title: Geometric classification and function approximation
description: Half-space tests, rectangle intersections, region unions and sums of pulses.
source_short: Lecture 2 / PDF pp.100,108-109,115-116 / original study examples
source: Lecture 2 - Logistic Regression + Neural Network.pdf, pages 100, 108-109 and 115-116.

pages.title: Turn inequalities into neuron tests
pages.subtitle: A half-space is the set of points on one side of a line, including the line here.
blocks: Study region: the closed rectangle 1 <= x <= 3 and 0 <= y <= 2. We need all four conditions to hold.
H(s) = 1 when s >= 0, else 0. This applies the half-space construction in Lecture 2, page 100.

pages.title: Require all four tests at the output
pages.subtitle: Lecture 2, page 108 combines half-space decisions using AND.
blocks: The four hidden neurons turn geometric tests into bits. The output checks those bits, not the original x and y values.
Their weights for (x, y) and biases are: (1, 0), -1; (-1, 0), 3; (0, 1), 0; (0, -1), 2.
Because equality passes each test, the rectangle includes its edges and corners.

pages.title: Inside: point (2, 1)
pages.subtitle: Evaluate every half-space, then combine their Boolean outputs.
blocks: A single failed boundary test rejects the point. Scores equal to zero pass because H(0) = 1.

pages.title: Left of the region: point (0, 1)
pages.subtitle: Evaluate every half-space, then combine their Boolean outputs.
blocks: A single failed boundary test rejects the point. Scores equal to zero pass because H(0) = 1.

pages.title: Above the region: point (2, 3)
pages.subtitle: Evaluate every half-space, then combine their Boolean outputs.
blocks: A single failed boundary test rejects the point. Scores equal to zero pass because H(0) = 1.

pages.title: At a corner: point (1, 0)
pages.subtitle: Evaluate every half-space, then combine their Boolean outputs.
blocks: A single failed boundary test rejects the point. Scores equal to zero pass because H(0) = 1.

pages.title: Picture the rectangle and its test points
pages.subtitle: The shaded region includes all four edges.
blocks: The corner (1, 0) passes both equality tests. The points (0, 1) and (2, 3) fail a different half-space each.

pages.title: Combine separate regions using OR
pages.subtitle: Lecture 2, page 109: accept a point if either region accepts it.
blocks: R2 is the closed rectangle 5 <= x <= 6, 0 <= y <= 2.
For (4,1): R1 = H(3 - 3.5) = 0 and R2 = H(3 - 3.5) = 0. U = H(0 + 0 - 0.5) = 0. The gap stays outside.

pages.title: A pulse is the difference of two steps
pages.subtitle: Lecture 2, page 115 uses two threshold neurons and a summing output.
blocks: The interval [a, b) includes a but excludes b. At b, the second step turns on and cancels the first.
This differs from our closed rectangle: pulse subtraction intentionally switches the output off at the right endpoint.

pages.title: Add two scaled pulses
pages.subtitle: Our study function has height 2 on [0,1) and height 0.5 on [1,3).
blocks: Hidden outputs are H(x), H(x-1), H(x-3). Final weights are (2, -1.5, -0.5) and bias 0.
The final output is a LINEAR sum, not another threshold. Thresholding it would lose the requested heights.

pages.title: Calculate pulse values: -0.5, 0, 0.5
pages.subtitle: First threshold the hidden scores, then take the unthresholded weighted sum.

pages.title: Calculate pulse values: 1, 2, 3
pages.subtitle: First threshold the hidden scores, then take the unthresholded weighted sum.

pages.title: Read the endpoints on the graph
pages.subtitle: Filled circles are included; open circles are excluded at each jump.
blocks: At x = 1 the first pulse ends and the second begins: f(1) = 0.5. At x = 3 both contributions cancel: f(3) = 0.
Narrow, scaled pulses are building blocks for approximation (page 116). This finite example is not a proof that one fixed small network exactly fits every function.

pages.title: Your turn: shift the region and pulses
pages.subtitle: Use the same H(0) = 1 convention.
blocks: A. Build the closed rectangle -1 <= x <= 1 and 2 <= y <= 4. Write its four hidden tests and AND output. Classify (-1,2), (0,3), (2,3).
B. Build a function of height 1.5 on [-1,0) and height 3 on [0,2), zero elsewhere. Give the three hidden steps, output weights and bias.
Calculate the function at x = -1, 0, 1 and 2. Show the hidden outputs before the weighted sum.
Do not threshold the final function-approximation output.

pages.title: Practice answer: the shifted rectangle
pages.subtitle: Translate each lower and upper bound separately.
blocks: The first point is an included corner. The last point fails the x <= 1 test.

pages.title: Practice answer: derive the pulse weights
pages.subtitle: Combine the repeated step at x = 0 before reading off the weights.
blocks: Hidden steps: H(x+1), H(x), H(x-2). Weights: (1.5, 1.5, -3), bias 0.
